Repair round: fixing the compile errors in `ThemeContrastTest.kt` only. Root cause: `org.junit.Assert.fail(...)` returns Java `void`, which Kotlin sees as `Unit` — not `Nothing` — so `tokens[name] ?: fail(...)` types `value` as `Any`, breaking `ushr` and the `== 0xFF` comparison. I'm also fixing a latent runtime crash in the token parser: `toInt(16)` throws `NumberFormatException` for any 8-digit hex ≥ `0x80000000` (every real Compose token is `0xFF......`), which would abort the oracle on harness failure instead of evaluating it. `toLong(16).toInt()` preserves the exact same Int value (two's-complement wrap), so assertions and strictness are unchanged.

**What I fixed:**
1. **Line 115-116 compile errors (root cause):** `org.junit.Assert.fail()` is a Java `void` method, which Kotlin types as `Unit` — not `Nothing` — so `tokens[name] ?: fail(...)` inferred `value: Any`, making `ushr` unresolved and `alpha == 0xFF` invalid. Replaced with `?: throw AssertionError("missing Theme.kt token $name")` — same missing-token failure condition and message.
2. **Latent runtime crash in token parser (affected this test's own oracle):** `toInt(16)` throws `NumberFormatException` for any 8-digit hex ≥ `0x80000000` (every real Compose token is `0xFF......`). Changed to `toLong(16).toInt()` — produces the identical `0xAARRGGBB` Int (two's-complement wrap), so contrast values are bit-for-bit unchanged. Flagging as an assumption: I widened this beyond the literal compiler errors because without it the test aborts on harness error rather than evaluating P9.
